text:
We priced "Mount Fuji view" rooms at Lake Kawaguchi for the same December night. The view itself cost ¥8,280 for two, but only one of three listings actually promised it 👇

🤔 Guess first, then check the answer 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kawaguchiko-fuji-view-room-what-you-buy

🏨 THE ROOM NAME IS THE PROMISE

1️⃣ A hotel with Fuji in its name still sold garden- and courtyard-view rooms. The room type called "Mt.Fuji View" (36 m²) was ¥61,020 with breakfast for two; the same-size garden-view twin was ¥52,740.

2️⃣ "Room selected at check-in" means the hotel picks on arrival. At one lakeside ryokan that was ¥47,500 with breakfast, against ¥39,330 for a room sold as "No View". You pay more, but nothing is promised.

3️⃣ What that ryokan does promise is shared: a 7th-floor bath over the lake, open 5:00–10:00 and 15:00–24:00.

🌅 THE FREE VERSION

🚶 A 15 m² twin by the lake was ¥14,910 with breakfast, served from 6:30. Walk out at first light to the Kawaguchiko Ohashi Bridge, which has a footpath, and Ubuyagasaki at its north end, about 1.6 km from the station.

✅ OUR TAKE

If Fuji from the bed is the point of the trip, pay for the room type that names it and compare it with the same-size room in the same hotel. If you'd rather spend the money elsewhere, take the simple room and the bridge.

☁️ Cloud can hide Fuji completely, and the paid rooms we checked had to be cancelled a week ahead. That's when the free viewpoint looks smartest.
